name: Result builder
first: A type whose static methods swiftc calls to combine the lines of a body of code into one value, so that the body lists its parts with no return.

dependsOn.why: A result builder changes how swiftc builds the body of a function, and its methods are functions.
dependsOn.whyInExample: `@ListBuilder` changes how swiftc builds the body of the function `packing()`.

dependsOn.why: The result builder in the example is a structure.

sil.shows: swiftc built the body of packing() as a call of buildBlock.

what.is: A result builder is a type marked `@resultBuilder`, whose static methods combine several values into one. Writing the builder's name as an attribute before a function, as `@ListBuilder`, lets the function's body list values one per line, with no `return`. swiftc turns those lines into a call of the builder's `buildBlock`.
what.afterExample: The body of `packing()` lists three strings and has no `return`. `ListBuilder` combines them into one array, which line 17 prints.
what.problem: Some values are built from many parts, such as a list of things to pack, or the views of a screen. Written as one call, they need commas, brackets, and a `return`. A result builder lets the code list the parts one per line, and builds the value from them.
what.how: When swiftc builds the program, it changes the body of `packing()`: it collects the value of each line, and passes them all to the `buildBlock` of `ListBuilder`, whose result the function returns. A builder can have more static methods, such as one for if statements, and swiftc calls each one where the body needs it.

when.text: Use one where a value is a list of parts that read more clearly one per line than as one call. SwiftUI builds the body of every view with its own result builder, the view builder.
Don't write one for a list that ordinary code makes as clearly, such as an array literal in brackets: the builder is one more type to read.

parts.name: The attribute `@resultBuilder`, line 1
parts.text: The attribute `@resultBuilder` makes `ListBuilder` a result builder. Its name can then be written as an attribute, and swiftc calls its methods. They are marked `static`: a static method belongs to the type itself, so swiftc calls it without making an instance of `ListBuilder`.

parts.name: The method `buildBlock`, lines 3 to 7
parts.text: The static method `buildBlock` combines the values of a block, such as the body of `packing()`. Its parameter `items`, on line 4, has the type `String...`: the three dots let a call pass any number of strings, which the method gets as an array. It returns that array.

parts.name: The attribute `@ListBuilder`, line 10
parts.text: Writing a result builder's name as an attribute before a function makes swiftc build the function's body with that builder. Each line of the body, such as `"Socks"`, is a value for the builder, and the body needs no `return`.

steps.text: swiftc built the body of `packing()` with `ListBuilder`, so the three strings on lines 12 to 14 are not separate statements. They are the arguments of one call of `buildBlock`.
`buildBlock` gets the three strings as the array `items`, and line 6 returns it. `packing()` returns that array.

end.text: swiftc turned the body of `packing()` into one call of `buildBlock`, which combined its three lines into one array.
